summary: Eisei Kojima was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as professor at Ryukoku University (circa 1951–1974) and as president of Doho University (circa 1975–1979).

Eisho Nasu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ronald Y. Nakasone, Judith A. Berling, Clare Fischer, and Lewis Lancaster. He served as Assistant Professor and Rev. Yoshitaka Tamai Professor of Jodo Shin Studies at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (circa 2000–2011).

Eishu Miyazaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (circa 1933–1936) and under Gyōō Kageyama. He later held academic posts at Rissho University (circa 1949–1984) and Minobusan University (circa 1988–1992).
Eishun Fushimi works in the fields of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson.

Eiun Hino is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's program at the University of Tokyo (circa 2004–2006). He later held appointments as a project researcher at the University of Tokyo and as an assistant professor at Musashino University (circa 2017–2020).

Ekai Kawaguchi studied Tibetology and Buddhism at Gyosei Shoin, Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College under multiple teachers. He held posts at Toyo University (1916), Taisho University (circa 1926–1933), and Toyo Bunko (1940).

Eki Nakayama is a researcher in Buddhist studies. Nakayama held a post at Kyoto University until 2020 and served as a DC2 fellow with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science from circa 2018 to 2020.
Ekkyo Uno is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Uno held posts as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji-ha Shogakuin until 1998.

Eleanor Rosch is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Reed College (circa 1959–1963) and Harvard University (circa 1965–1969), and held a faculty post at the University of California, Berkeley (circa 1971–1989).
Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetologist who held academic posts at the University of Bonn and Sapienza University of Rome, where she taught Michela Clemente.

Elena France Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University by 1998, studying under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey, committee members John J. Makransky and John B. Carman, and teacher Masatoshi Nagatomi.

Elena Mucciarelli studied at the University of Tübingen (circa 2008–2010), where she later held a post from 2016 to 2017. An Indologist, she was Assistant Professor for Hinduism in the Sanskrit Tradition and Gonda Lecturer at the University of Groningen in 2020.

Eli Franco works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at La Trobe University, Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (1989–1990), Kyoto University (1994), the Austrian Academy of Sciences (circa 2000–2005), and became a professor at Leipzig University around 2007.

Elijah Ary studied Tibetology and Buddhist studies at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University (PhD circa 2007). His supervisors included Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp, alongside teachers Geshe Karma Sonam, Anne M. Blackburn, and Charles Hallisey.

Eliot Deutsch was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Columbia University (until circa 1960). He was a professor at the University of Hawaii (circa 1967–2019) and edited Philosophy East and West (1967–1988), holding posts at Harvard, Chicago, and Cambridge.

Elisa Freschi is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under doctoral supervisor Raffaele Torella (completed circa 2006). She held positions at Sapienza University of Rome, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, IKGA, and served as university assistant at the University of Vienna (circa 2012–2019).

Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Würzburg (circa 1958–1963) and the University of Münster (circa 1963–1970). She held posts at the University of Notre Dame (circa 1970–1985) and Harvard University (circa 1986–2021).

Elizabeth Ann Cecil earned degrees from Hastings College, University of Tennessee, and Brown University under James L. Fitzgerald. Specializing in Indology, religious studies, and archaeology, she held posts at Groningen, Baroda, Leiden, and became Assistant Professor at Florida State University in 2019.

Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford (circa 1994–1999) under the supervision of Alexis Sanderson and studied under Harunaga Isaacson.

Elizabeth Errington is a specialist in archaeology and Buddhist studies who completed her graduate work at SOAS University of London under Adrian David Hugh Bivar (circa 1978–1987). She served as a curator of pre-Islamic South and Central Asian coins at the British Museum.
